title: Fasolada (Greek white bean soup)

ingredients.name: dried white beans (haricot or cannellini), soaked overnight
extra virgin olive oil, plus more to serve

steps: Drain the soaked beans, put them in a large pot with plenty of fresh water and boil for 10 minutes. Drain again and discard the water, which helps make the beans easier to digest.
In the same pot, warm half of the olive oil and cook the onion, carrot and celery for about 5 minutes until they begin to soften, then add the garlic for a minute.
Stir in the tomato paste, then add the beans, chopped tomatoes, bay leaves and oregano, and cover with about 1.5 litres of hot water.
Bring to a boil, then lower the heat and simmer, partly covered, for 1 to 1.5 hours until the beans are completely tender and the broth is thick.
Season with salt and pepper only near the end, add the remaining olive oil and simmer a few minutes more; mash a few beans against the side of the pot if you want a thicker soup.
Serve hot with parsley, a thread of olive oil, olives, feta and crusty bread.

title: Kleftiko (Greek slow-roasted lamb with potatoes)

ingredients.name: lamb shoulder or leg, on the bone, cut into large pieces
large onion, cut into thick wedges
red or green bell pepper, cut into chunks
kefalotyri or feta, cut into slabs (optional)

steps: Mix the olive oil, lemon juice and zest, wine, oregano, plenty of salt and pepper and half of the garlic. Rub this over the lamb and marinate for at least 4 hours, ideally overnight.
Heat the oven to 160 C (140 C fan). Lay a large sheet of baking paper over a deep roasting tin, with enough overhang to fold over the top later.
Spread the potatoes, onion, pepper, remaining garlic and bay leaves on the paper, season, and place the lamb on top. Pour over the marinade.
Add the cheese slabs if using, then fold the paper up over the food and wrap it into a tight parcel, covering with foil if you do not have enough paper.
Roast for about 3 to 3.5 hours, until the lamb is falling off the bone and the potatoes have soaked up the juices.
Open the parcel for the last 20 minutes at 200 C so the top browns lightly. Serve straight from the tin with a salad and lemon wedges.

title: Melomakarona (Greek honey and walnut Christmas cookies)
steps: Heat the oven to 180 C (160 C fan). Whisk the olive oil, sugar, orange juice, zest and brandy together until the sugar dissolves.
Mix the flour, semolina, cinnamon, cloves, baking powder and baking soda, then add to the wet mixture and fold gently into a soft dough. Do not overwork it or the cookies will be tough.
Shape the dough into small oval cookies about 6 cm long and place them on lined trays, pressing the tops lightly with a fork.
Bake for 20 to 25 minutes until golden, then cool on a rack.
Meanwhile boil the honey with the water for 5 minutes and skim off the foam, then keep it warm over low heat.
Dip the cooled cookies into the warm syrup for about 30 seconds each, turn them once, and lift them onto a rack to drain.
Sprinkle with the chopped walnuts while still sticky and leave to set. They taste better after a day.

title: Skordalia (Greek garlic and potato dip)

ingredients.name: floury potatoes, peeled and cut into chunks
garlic, crushed to a paste with salt
white wine vinegar or lemon juice

steps: Boil the potatoes in salted water for about 20 minutes, until completely soft. Drain well and let the steam escape for a couple of minutes.
While they are still warm, pass the potatoes through a ricer or mash them very thoroughly in a bowl. A food processor makes the mix gluey, so avoid it.
Crush the garlic with a little salt to a smooth paste and stir it into the potatoes.
Beat in the olive oil in a thin stream, a little at a time, as if making mayonnaise, until the mixture is creamy and glossy.
Add the vinegar or lemon juice, then taste and adjust the garlic, salt and acidity. Thin with a spoonful of warm water if it is too stiff.
Serve at room temperature with fried or roasted fish, beetroot, or fried courgette and aubergine slices.

title: Spanakorizo (Greek spinach and rice)

ingredients.name: fresh spinach, washed and roughly chopped (or 500 g frozen)

steps: Warm the olive oil in a wide pot and cook the onion and spring onions gently for about 8 minutes, until soft and golden.
Stir in the tomato paste and cook for a minute, then add the spinach in batches, letting each batch wilt before adding the next.
Cook the spinach for about 5 minutes, until most of its liquid has come out.
Add the rice, season with salt and pepper and pour in about 400 ml of hot water. Stir once and bring to a boil.
Cover, reduce the heat to low and cook for 15 to 18 minutes until the rice is tender and the liquid is absorbed; add a splash more hot water if it dries out too soon.
Stir in the dill, mint and lemon juice, rest for 5 minutes, and serve warm or at room temperature with feta and an extra drizzle of olive oil.
